title: Excluded Source Record
description: One entry in metadata/excluded-sources.json. This is the machine-readable form of a collection-ethics decision documented in knowledge/security/llm-security/excluded-sources.md. It exists so the decision fails a build instead of depending on every future contributor remembering it: SECURITY.md declares these exclusions hard, and a hard exclusion that nothing enforces degrades on the first well-intentioned addition of a popular repository.

slug.description: owner/name. Matched as a whole slug, never as a bare name, so a repository called `skills` cannot implicate every file that uses the word.

kind.description: What sort of source the exclusion covers. A repository exclusion is enforced against seeds.json and repositories.json; the others are enforced against citation and link paths.

category.description: Which of the hard exclusions in SECURITY.md's collection-ethics list this entry instantiates. Constrained to that list so an exclusion cannot be recorded against a category the policy does not declare.

reason.description: What the source actually contains that makes it ineligible. Long enough that a bare label will not do: the point of recording the reason is that a future contributor can see the decision was made about this content, not about the topic.

decision.description: Only `excluded` is valid. A source that is merely risky belongs in the corpus with a confidence and a license_risk, not here; putting it here would let the file drift into a general watchlist that nobody treats as binding.

decided_on.description: When the decision was made. An exclusion with no date cannot be revisited, and cannot be distinguished from an oversight.

observed_stars.description: Star count at the time of the decision, recorded deliberately. The point is to make the tradeoff explicit: these are among the most-starred repositories in their category and this knowledge base still does not use them, so a future reader who notices the omission has the answer.

prohibits.description: What the exclusion forbids, in plain language. Each entry names a concrete action rather than restating the decision, so that a contributor can tell whether what they are about to do is covered.

permitted_mentions.description: Where naming the source is allowed. An exclusion that could not be named could not be documented, and a contributor who cannot see it will rediscover the repository and add it in good faith.

documented_in.description: Path to the prose reasoning. Must exist; validate_links.py checks repository paths named in prose, and this one is named here.
